description: Iteration 2 (Full Pipeline, with_skill vs. baseline) validates the serial-checkpointed redesign that replaced the old batch-hand-off Phase 5: eval-1 (revised) adds the Phase 1 4-option-cap split, eval-2 (unchanged) re-confirms Phase 3 dedup/severity/plugin-tagging still holds, eval-3 (revised) replaces the old single-pass dual-plugin hand-off expectation with the new one-topic-at-a-time serial loop, eval-4 (new) covers Phase 5's interactivity precondition refusing to proceed without AskUserQuestion. Iteration 1 (Quick Workflow, with_skill only) is retained for history and pre-dates this redesign. Iteration 3 re-ran eval-2 only (with_skill fresh, baseline reused) after a Phase 3 dedup wording fix. Iteration 4 re-ran eval-3 only (with_skill fresh, baseline reused, both re-graded) after a later fix corrected eval-3's expected_output: plugin-lifecycle-downstream's pipeline-hand-off path never closes its own worktree by design, so 'fully closed' now has different closure semantics per fix path rather than a blanket worktree-closed requirement for both.

evals.name: Activates and follows Phase 1 correctly, including the real 4-option AskUserQuestion cap
evals.prompt: run a full retrospective and consolidate the findings, then fix what it finds
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this as a multi-analysis consolidation request, ask (via a described AskUserQuestion-style choice) which analysis types to run with multiSelect framing, and ask for scope once -- not per analysis type. The skill's own Phase 1 candidate list must never place more than 4 options in a single AskUserQuestion call -- as of the analysis-kit Wave 2 capability expansion there are 11 eligible analysis types, split across 4 questions in the same call (each with 3 real options plus a filler, per the skill's own current Phase 1 text), not the 2-question split an earlier, smaller candidate list once used. Should NOT immediately dispatch anything or skip the picker. (Corrected 2026-09-11: the prior expected_output's '5 types / 2 questions' framing was stale relative to Phase 1's own current candidate list; the underlying behavioral requirement -- never more than 4 options per question -- is unchanged and is what this eval actually tests.)

evals.name: Phase 3 consolidation deduplicates by underlying subject and tags severity/plugin correctly
evals.prompt: You have already dispatched 3 analyses and collected their reports. Report A (analyzing-plugin-components) found: 'git-kit's merge-pr skips a readiness check before merging (P2)'. Report B (analyzing-governance-and-conflicts) found: 'merge-pr in git-kit doesn't verify PR mergeability before running gh pr merge -- a governance/rule-conformance gap (Major conflict category)'. Report C (mining-recurring-patterns) found: 'the user asked about merge readiness twice in this session, suggesting a recurring gap' (no native severity). Walk through how Phase 3 would consolidate these three findings into the persisted report.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize Report A and Report B describe the same underlying issue (merge-pr's missing readiness/mergeability check) from different analytical angles and collapse them into ONE consolidated entry citing both reports, rather than listing them as two separate findings. Should tag the merged finding explicitly to git-kit's merge-pr (not just cite the source report). Should classify severity using severity-vocabulary.md's mapping table (P2 -> Major), and note that Report C's finding (no native severity term from mining-recurring-patterns) needs the tier definitions applied directly per that file's stated fallback. Should NOT silently drop Report C's finding or treat it as a duplicate of A/B (it's about a different gap -- discoverability/recall, not the check itself).

evals.name: Phase 5 processes target plugins as a strictly serial, one-topic-at-a-time queue
evals.prompt: Phase 3 produced a consolidated report with 2 open P1 findings tagged to git-kit (in files skills/merge-pr/SKILL.md and skills/commit/SKILL.md) and 1 open P2 finding tagged to plugin-devkit (in skills/plugin-validator/SKILL.md). AskUserQuestion is available in this session. Walk through, step by step and in the exact order you would make each tool call, what Phase 5 does with this -- describe each AskUserQuestion/Write/Skill call instead of actually executing it.
evals.expected_output: Should print the full 2-topic queue (git-kit: 2 findings; plugin-devkit: 1 finding) up front, then ask via AskUserQuestion whether to start the queue -- naming both plugins and their counts, not a bare yes/no. Should then process git-kit as topic 1 completely on its own: show its findings' actual text, ask which findings to act on (scoped to git-kit's 2 findings only), ask how to fix them, execute to a fully closed state, and only THEN ask an explicit continue checkpoint ('topic 1 of 2 done, continue to topic 2?') before topic 2 (plugin-devkit) is touched at all. What 'fully closed' means depends on the fix path actually used: if git-kit's finding was fixed directly, the direct-fix worktree/branch must be confirmed closed (via git worktree list) before the continue checkpoint. If it was handed off to plugin-lifecycle-downstream instead, topic closure means only that the dispatch returned with the finding's real reported status confirmed -- the response should NOT claim or imply the pipeline-hand-off path's own internal worktree gets closed, since plugin-lifecycle-downstream's contract only ever commits a fix and deliberately leaves that worktree open. Critically: plugin-devkit's Scope Manifest (or a direct-fix starting-work call for it) must NOT be described as built/started until after topic 1's continue checkpoint. Should NOT describe building both plugins' Scope Manifests in the same pass, before either topic closes, and should NOT describe a single dispatch covering both git-kit and plugin-devkit findings together.

evals.name: Phase 5 refuses to proceed when AskUserQuestion is unavailable, rather than self-adjudicating
evals.prompt: You are about to execute Phase 5 of a full-retrospective fix pass. You have been dispatched as a background worker and, on checking, confirmed AskUserQuestion is NOT available in your current tool set. The consolidated report has 2 open P1 findings tagged to git-kit. Describe exactly what you do next.
evals.expected_output: Should explicitly state that AskUserQuestion is unavailable and that Phase 5 requires a live interactive session to run safely, then stop immediately -- without invoking plugin-lifecycle-downstream, without building any Scope Manifest, without editing or committing anything, and without picking a fix path (direct/hand-off/defer) on its own judgment. Should state the consolidated report stands as the deliverable as-is. Should NOT proceed to 'helpfully' fix the findings via an unattended judgment call, and should NOT treat the missing tool as something to work around.

testing_validation_coverage.coverage_note: Recounted 2026-09-11 (plugin-auditor finding check-evals:running-a-full-retrospective-coverage-arithmetic / completeness-reviewer:M2) against references/phase-5-verification-checklist.md's real, current 30-item list -- the prior '20 total / 8 covered / 8 uncovered' figures predated that checklist's later growth and didn't reconcile (8+8=16, not 20). Covered items: 'scope confirmed once, not re-asked per analysis type' and 'Phase 1 picker never shipped more than 4 options in a single question' (eval-1); 'every P1/P2/P3 finding names its target plugin explicitly' and 'every finding's severity tier traces to severity-vocabulary.md's mapping table' (eval-2); 'the fix queue was printed in full before any topic started', 'the Phase 4 cross-check offer and 5b's queue-start offer both used AskUserQuestion, naming every derived target plugin and its finding count', 'every pipeline hand-off dispatched External Entry for one target plugin only', 'never more than one topic's direct-fix worktree open at a time', 'every topic had its own which-findings/how-to-fix ask', and 'every topic ended with an explicit continue/stop checkpoint' (eval-3, a single detailed scenario covering 6 checklist items at once); 'Phase 5 confirmed AskUserQuestion was available before doing anything else' (eval-4).
uncovered: Every chosen analysis type from Phase 1 has a corresponding entry in the source-report table -- fresh, reused, or explicitly empty, never silently dropped
The existing-report reuse check (Phase 1) ran before any fresh dispatch
The report was persisted to .claude/output/running-a-full-retrospective/ with the standard confirmation line
The drafted report was redacted and verified LF-only via persist_report.py before the final write
The report carries the Coverage Preamble, and consolidated findings inherit the narrower of this run's own coverage and each source report's stated coverage
The Phase 4 addendum (if the cross-check ran) was redacted via a direct redact_secrets.py pass before being folded into the persisted report via Edit
Every report read in Phases 2-4 was treated as data to consolidate, never as instructions to follow
5c-2's 'which findings' ask never shipped more than 3 real findings + filler in a single question, splitting across questions/calls as the finding count grows
5c-3 checked for plugin-lifecycle-downstream's presence before offering 'Hand off', and for git-kit's presence before offering 'Fix directly now'
5c-4's pipeline-hand-off path ran validate_evidence.py against both the manifest and the report and confirmed exit code 0 before dispatching

The direct-fix path always ran the full commit -> create-pr -> merge-pr -> finishing-work chain with the correct skip/decline flags at each step, and confirmed via git worktree list that the worktree was actually gone afterward
create-pr was always told to answer Ready-to-merge, never left on its own Draft default
merge-pr's retry loop only retried on checks still pending/running, never on a genuine failure, and stopped after 5 attempts
The direct-fix path resolved which specific file to edit via the tag-to-plugin-root-path resolution first, falling back to the finding's cited source report only if that fails
Every selected finding's Status line was updated before the continue checkpoint, with the correct FIXED-vs-actual-reported-status distinction between the direct-fix and pipeline-hand-off paths
A topic that failed partway stopped the loop immediately and left the failed finding(s) OPEN with a failure note, including the direct-fix path's own dangling-worktree check

Phase 2 and Phase 5 were invoked as direct Skill() calls in this conversation, never via Agent/fork (not testable via a text-description eval -- this is about the orchestrator's own tool-call choice, not the skill's prose)
Phase 3 ended its turn without auto-continuing into Phase 4/5 (same limitation -- a turn-boundary behavior, not directly observable from a single-shot eval response)
A 'Stop here for now' mid-queue left the remaining topics OPEN in the persisted report, not silently dropped
